page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this server includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 24 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI for vector calculations, alongside AES cryptography acceleration. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves average performance in single-core metrics, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1572.39 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1309.0. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also register average throughput. However, multi-core and memory subsystem benchmarks are comparatively weak. The stress-ng multi-core performance of 4147.67 and Geekbench multi-core score of 2855.0 fall into the lower percentiles, while memory bandwidth tests for large uncached blocks show weak throughput at 28.26 GB/sec for reads and 24.11 GB/sec for writes.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2-standard-4 provides dedicated compute resources suitable for workloads that rely heavily on single-threaded execution and vector instructions rather than massive parallelization. Given the weak multi-core scaling and database performance, it is less suited for heavy database operations or high-throughput web serving. Appropriate workloads include lightweight single-threaded processing, basic text processing, and small-scale LLM inference text generation, where it achieves an average speed of 74.92 tokens per second on a 135M model.
